actions: Open a fresh home; exercise setup, provider-key entry, walkthrough Next/Back/Skip/reopen, and empty-state Create.
expected: No blank or permanently connecting screen; missing prerequisites are actionable; setup persists.

actions: Open every top-level tab, overflow menu, hide/show/reorder tabs, reload, use Back/Forward and a direct entity link.
expected: Selected view and scope match the URL; hidden tabs remain discoverable; no offscreen controls.

actions: Create a worker from New worker; exercise name validation, provider/model, cwd autocomplete, template, branch and worktree choices; cancel a second creation.
expected: Exactly one durable worker; correct provider/cwd/branch; cancellation creates nothing; no false successful start.

actions: Start, send a short task, observe running/working/idle, stop, restart and reopen terminal.
expected: Real process and displayed state agree; output resumes once; unrelated workers are untouched.

actions: Exercise every card-menu and peek-menu action, rename, duplicate/clone, pin/unpin, archive/restore and search; verify aliases and copied links.
expected: Actions produce the named effect; rename preserves board/history identity; copies do not silently share identity.

actions: Edit description, label, cwd, branch, model, provider, effort, permissions, isolation and MCP; reload and restore.
expected: Durable values match UI; restart/apply timing is explained; prior task context is retained.

actions: At global/group/worker levels edit memory, instructions, environment, rules, connectors, skin and gates; override then Inherit.
expected: Source and effective value agree; sibling scope is unaffected; Inherit removes only the override.

actions: Create an isolated test worker and compare discovery, incoming peer messaging, harness and automation with a normal worker.
expected: Isolation effects are visible and enforced; it cannot auto-pick up normal board work.

actions: Filter/search/group/sort/freeze the worker list; put one worker on one task then let it finish.
expected: Exactly the claimed task is Working now; counts, ordering and final idle state agree with authoritative data.

actions: Create/rename a group, add/remove workers, edit scoped configuration, switch scope, then remove the empty test group.
expected: Membership and inherited settings persist; no cross-group data leakage or accidental mass mutation.

actions: Submit one instruction with at least three distinct deliverables and dependencies through the worker composer.
expected: Separate actionable tasks are created and linked to the source message; no untouched capture shell counts as work.

actions: Create through the UI with notes, owner, group, due time and gate; reopen, edit, search, filter, switch views and export Markdown/JSON.
expected: Exactly one task persists, all fields and export match, empty search has a useful state, cancel preserves old values.

actions: Open old/new deep links; inspect status, next action, owner, blockers, history, evidence and outputs; follow worker and file links.
expected: The card alone explains work and next action; the exact linked entity opens; details fit every viewport.

actions: Create custom test columns and gates; reorder them; edit a gate; transition a scratch task with a missing condition, then supply real proof.
expected: The refusal names the unmet gate; permitted transition records actor/time; custom terminal state is honored.

actions: Create backlog work with a clear next action; leave the observer idle for several driver ticks. Exercise both Backlog and Todo on each of two real workers, with dependencies in opposite initial-state order and no chat prompt, observer claim, evidence write or status advancement.
expected: Work progresses to todo and doing without observer nudges; history attributes the promotion. Every original seeded ID reaches an evidenced terminal state; completing only one worker is INCOMPLETE. Retain timelines for starvation or acknowledgement-generated work.

actions: Create three scratch backlog cards due seven, three and one days ago, with a deterministic tied-due pair.
expected: Promotion is oldest due first, then stable ID order; partial promotion explains rate limit or WIP.

actions: Queue work behind a claimed task; attempt a second claim and a competing-worker claim.
expected: One owner/lease wins; blocked work explains WIP; after completion the next task starts once.

actions: Create parent/children and a blocked dependency; attempt a cycle; complete children through real work.
expected: Cycles are rejected; parents remain blocked until all prerequisites meet their required terminal conditions.

actions: Attempt done without an artifact, without evidence, and with a false gate acknowledgment; then supply real results.
expected: All invalid closures are refused visibly; legitimate closure preserves command, result and accessible output.

actions: Create a genuine missing-input or dependency blocker; inspect card and worker; provide the input through normal UI.
expected: Blocked state names reason/owner/next action; work resumes without resetting unrelated tasks.

actions: Run the three-part live journey: implement sum, test it, add non-finite validation, retest, produce HTML and Markdown results.
expected: Actual files change, independent tests pass, tasks finish with evidence; generated HTML renders its unique run marker.

actions: Independently run the artifact tests, inspect its rendered result, verify task, then reopen with a concrete correction and repeat.
expected: Verified is backed by fresh checks; reopened work is driven back to a terminal state; history retains both cycles.

actions: Archive/restore and discard only test cards; inspect terminal availability; try the column migration dialog then Cancel.
expected: No unintended card moves; cancelled migration changes nothing; archived/discarded items remain traceable.

actions: Type/paste multiline text, expand composer, switch send modes, send once, inspect pending/sent/failed, retry a controlled failure.
expected: Exact text and origin reach the right worker once; drafts survive failures and worker switching.

actions: Send multipart work and inspect message card chips; open each child task and navigate back.
expected: Every durable card link opens the exact child and its state/artifacts; source kind and MSG ID remain truthful.

actions: In a test-only group make one worker request work from another, wait for completion/callback, inspect both boards.
expected: Own-board boundary enforced; links and callbacks preserve attribution; no duplicate unowned task escape.

actions: Open terminal/transcript; navigate earlier/later messages, source/content filters, Find, copy, path links and focus mode; test long output. For Gemini and Sonnet, send human and peer messages, produce enough output to require older-history loading, then find each exact message under its origin filter and open its linked task on desktop and phone.
expected: Scroll anchors and filter selection survive refresh; no cross-worker output/draft/card mixing; toolbar is reachable. Durable peer history must remain navigable after it leaves the live terminal frame; paint-log fallback cannot count as verified structured provider history.

actions: Start/pause/resume/seek/close read-aloud, change worker mid-playback, and interrupt playback.
expected: Player controls match audio state, stale playback stops appropriately, and no inaccessible overlay remains.

actions: Upload a text file, close peek mid-transfer, cancel another, force failure, retry and download.
expected: File bytes match; transfer survives closing; cancel is not an error; failed chip retains its retryable file.

actions: Browse scratch directories, breadcrumb, search, open text/image/PDF/HTML, edit/save/reopen, create/rename/delete scratch files.
expected: Correct file and content open; binary/large/missing files explain limitations; previews fit phone screens.

actions: Create/read/edit/delete worker memory, inspect inherited memory, search and reload; have worker use a unique fact.
expected: Version/content and effective scope persist; subsequent worker output uses the saved fact.

actions: Create schedule, choose worker/cadence/timezone, edit, disable/enable, run now, wait for natural fire, then delete.
expected: One attributed run per trigger; disabled schedule does not fire; history includes edited/deleted jobs.

actions: Open SYSTEM jobs, expand details, compare healthy/stalled/disabled jobs; use Run now only on the dedicated lab.
expected: UI agrees with registry/timestamps; stalled job is distinct; automation actually advances eligible tasks.

actions: Create/edit/move/delete a scratch calendar event; inspect all-day/timezone/day boundaries and exported iCal.
expected: UI and feed represent the same event and timezone; deletion removes only that event.

actions: Create test profile, start, navigate local artifact, view live screen, screenshot, history Back/Forward, open/close tab and stop.
expected: Real browser output updates; active/locked/unavailable states are distinguishable; process ends after Stop.

actions: Create/edit/discard a draft; with explicit test-recipient authorization send to a controlled sink and inspect Sent.
expected: Draft persists; actual test delivery and Sent agree; failure preserves draft and visible error.

actions: Add a test connector, configure scope, connect/disconnect, deny and expire auth, test and retry.
expected: Auth health and scoped availability are accurate; credentials are masked; revoked connector cannot act.

actions: Edit a test env variable/key through supported UI, reload, clear override, enter invalid value and test unavailable provider.
expected: Saved/effective config agree without stale refresh overwrite; absent/invalid key has a recoverable state.

actions: Create uniquely named worker/task/group/memory/file; search globally and within tabs, filters, zero results and deep links.
expected: Every supported entity type is findable and opens correct scope; unsupported search domains are recorded as gaps.

actions: Go offline, create three cards and edit existing work, reload offline, reconnect and wait for replay.
expected: Durable queue retains exact intent, server receives each mutation once, UI converges and queue drains.

actions: Open two clients; edit the same task and distinct tasks concurrently; reconnect a stale client.
expected: Visible revision conflict protects both drafts; unrelated changes converge with no lost update.

actions: Interrupt SSE without a clean close, cut network, restore; provoke bad auth and unavailable API.
expected: Status reflects usable data, zombie stream recovers, auth failure differs from retryable outage, no endless silent spinner.

actions: Install/open PWA, offline launch, cached-version upgrade, failure bar dismissal, save below banner.
expected: Upgrade does not lose drafts; failure explains offline limits; Save stays tappable on phone.

actions: Exercise every settings tab and control: theme, zoom, tabs, offline limits, device name, defaults, connections, About, devtools and walkthrough.
expected: Persisted controls survive reload; local-only settings remain local; modals close by keyboard and pointer.

actions: Run real work; inspect token/cost ledger, worker/task attribution, limits, budget exhaustion and recovery.
expected: Nonzero real usage appears under correct identity; unknown/unmeasured is not zero; budget stops and recovery are clear.

actions: Inspect logs search/filter/details, measured diagnostic endpoints, invariant failures and client action error.
expected: Failed actions produce an attributable diagnostic signal; measured/n_considered distinguish empty from unmeasured.

actions: Open Workspace grid, add/remove panes, resize/focus, switch worker; open map/graph and metrics filters.
expected: Pane identity remains correct; graph/metrics reflect scratch tasks and terminal states; no stale cross-worker data.

actions: Inspect MDAI, Proxies, Skills, Database, Torrents, journal/habits where enabled; use their creation/edit/cancel controls on test fixtures.
expected: Each advertised control works or explains its prerequisite; missing capabilities are recorded, not silently skipped.

actions: Invite test members/devices, restrict group access, edit concurrently, revoke one member and retest both clients.
expected: Authorized client continues; revoked client loses access; no hidden mutation leaks across scope.

actions: Repeat core task flow on installed providers; switch model/provider mid-work and inspect continuation, rate-limit recovery and cancellation.
expected: Same durable task context and identity survive supported swaps; unavailable providers remain INCOMPLETE.

actions: Restart only dedicated lab server and worker process during queued and active work; reconnect UI.
expected: Tasks/messages/files/gates persist; ownership reconciles; no duplicate execution; build identity brackets evidence.

actions: Inspect each checkpoint and every open dialog/popover across desktop, 375px, iPhone WebKit, light/dark, empty/populated/error/long text.
expected: No clipping/overlap or inaccessible action; focus/labels/keyboard/touch work; discovered controls have explicit effect-verification rows.

actions: Create author, reviewer and consumer in one test group. Each reads its own and peers’ actual tasks, identifies ownership/status/blockers and names the exact IDs in messages. Repeat discovery and peer task reads with a worker that has no group, in both directions.
expected: Roster and board facts are correct without operator-pasted task context; same-group access is a positive control.

actions: Place author in build and reviewer/consumer in quality. Discover peers, inspect permitted task context, request work and wait for response with normal open defaults.
expected: Actual originated peer messages cross groups; request and response identify the right cards and artifacts.

actions: Set a worker/group deny, attempt a new cross-group request, allow one destination, retry, clear override and inspect effective policy.
expected: Denied request is visibly refused with no delivered work; allowed destination succeeds; inheritance restores the documented default, not blanket access by accident.

actions: With initiation restricted, test a reply to an actual incoming request, an unsolicited new message, and a message to an isolated worker in the same group.
expected: Documented reply path works only with genuine inbound history; unsolicited initiation respects policy; isolation cannot be bypassed by group membership.

actions: Author supplies a deliberate empty-input defect and requests review. Reviewer discovers the task, independently runs the failing test, owns a review task and sends REVIEW_CHANGES.
expected: Reviewer is a different worker, cites actual task/file/failure, and the implementation cannot be treated as approved before repair.

actions: Author revises after reviewer feedback, records the changed artifact and tests, asks for re-review. Reviewer reruns tests and sends REVIEW_APPROVED.
expected: Durable message timestamps prove rejection precedes approval; approval refers to the revised work and actual successful tests, not the old artifact.

actions: Consumer reads author/reviewer tasks, creates its own dependent integration task, waits for approval, tests the artifact, and sends HANDOFF_DONE. After HANDOFF_DONE, observe three complete board-driver cycles with no new user input; record cycle boundaries, per-worker open task IDs, messages and model calls.
expected: Integration finishes after approval; linked task IDs belong to the correct peers; callback wakes requester and all three workers reach evidenced terminal states. A completion callback must not request another acknowledgement or manufacture another review task solely to process its receipt. Completion receipts do not generate recursively captured acknowledgement tasks; all original deliverables remain terminal and no new model turn exists solely to acknowledge a receipt.

surface: No peer ownership hijack or duplicate dispatch
actions: Two workers attempt to claim one task; repeat request/callback delivery; ask a peer for work without changing its owned task directly.
expected: One claim wins; one callback effect; task ownership and verified message origin stay accurate; duplicate work is not manufactured.

actions: Stop reviewer before request, resume it later; separately test archived, isolated, error and rate-limited reviewers. Also test host admission denial separately from provider quota exhaustion; retry in a dedicated lab only after the actual blocking condition clears.
expected: Requester shows who/what it awaits, retains its next action, avoids false completion, and resumes when the actual reviewer returns. Health may be OK while new worker admission is denied. Unavailable prerequisites remain BLOCKED/INCOMPLETE and never satisfy native delivery or task-completion assertions.

actions: Move reviewer between test groups or change its scope while a review is pending, then refresh both workers and both dashboard clients.
expected: Effective policy and peer awareness refresh; pending work remains attributable and either completes through permitted routing or visibly explains the new restriction.

actions: Inventory every run-owned entity; inspect all deliverables, verify results, stop/archive test workers and disable/delete test schedules.
expected: All requested work is terminal with proof; no active leases, duplicate dispatches or orphan jobs; unresolved work is explicitly failed/incomplete.

surface: Linked outcome board and task record
actions: Create an epic and linked dependent children; inspect evidence and acceptance criteria; follow task, message, file, file URL, HTTP URL and git commit links. Repeat at desktop and phone widths.
expected: Every link reaches its exact persisted target; evidence stays readable; no fabricated progress or overflow.

actions: Send one substantive request to two real Sonnet workers. Require worker-created epic/children, dependencies, source-message links, peer review, produced artifacts and exact execution evidence. Change Verified criteria mid-work; observe discovery, extra work and independent verification.
expected: Workers create the decomposition and satisfy the current gate. Every required deliverable reaches Verified. Stale acknowledgments fail, and no observer writes work evidence or closes deliverable cards.

actions: Edit inherited and overridden criteria before transition and after verification; retry an old checklist, then supply current checks; reload details.
expected: The effective gate is authoritative; changed criteria are visible; prior verification cannot silently claim the newer requirements.

actions: Create tasks through both the direct board API and six actual composer messages to a real worker: initial request, paraphrase, added context, revised requirements, independent UI outcome and separate-domain output. Use the real helper model and inspect task/message links in desktop and phone views.
expected: The six messages produce exactly three tasks. Paraphrase/context/refinement preserve one survivor ID, increasing revision, all four linked full source messages and original requirements. Logs must record measured create/append/update decisions. Distinct outcomes remain separate. No explicit task IDs, mocked classifier, observer board/history writes or manual completion can manufacture the result; unavailable comparison fails the live case.

actions: Send multiline text and an uploaded file; delay the server response, type a newer draft, reload, lose the response after delivery, retry, refuse submission and simulate full device storage. Inspect terminal and pending Messages. Fill the real browser storage quota with disposable caches, keep another draft and a pending message, then send a large message. Repeat with unrecoverable storage failure and inspect Sync diagnostics.
expected: Local persistence clears only the accepted draft immediately; attachment paths and one stable message ID survive retry/reload. Delivery requires a confirmed/deferred/deduplicated receipt. Refused or ambiguous operations remain reviewable and preserve ordering. Failed local storage keeps the draft and sends nothing. Cache pressure is reclaimed before local refusal, without discarding user intent. Normal sends keep Send stable and emit no queue/sync completion flash. Irrecoverable storage failures have precise, content-free diagnostics.

surface: Worker creation focus and explicit navigation
actions: Type the worker directory while initial focus is delayed; reload a saved terminal and select the Workers tab before restoration runs.
expected: Directory typing stays in its selected field. Explicit navigation cancels a delayed old-terminal restoration, and the requested main page remains usable.

actions: Enter short and long multiline drafts; toggle Send/Queue on desktop, 320px mobile, iPhone Safari, landscape and reduced keyboard viewports. Open Attach file and cancel the chooser, then clear the draft.
expected: Phone inputs occupy the full composer width with aligned 44px controls below. Actions and attachment menus remain inside the viewport, mode changes and cancelling file selection preserve text, and clearing a long draft reclaims its height.

actions: Edit a task without saving; follow a worker deep link in the same page; return to the task.
expected: The previous task overlay no longer intercepts worker actions, and the unsaved task edit survives.

actions: On a real Gemini worker with existing peer messages, choose New conversation, upload a file and submit a task. Restart normally afterward. Repeat the fresh reset contract for Codex.
expected: A fresh launch never resumes the prior provider ID. Uploaded input reaches the actual provider and its receipt task reaches an evidenced terminal state. A normal restart retains the newly created conversation identity. A following ordinary message is durably accepted during restart, retries produce one queue copy, and delivery waits for the replacement process.

actions: Capture an assignment with required file paths and schema beyond its 300-character card preview. Read it through board show, then its --messages option, and recover the worker after restart.
expected: The compact view exposes source message IDs and a supported full-read command. Full linked assignments preserve attachment paths and acceptance criteria; recovery does not guess from truncated text or search terminal logs.

actions: Create a real board revision conflict, go offline, inspect its review link, enqueue a second edit, dismiss only the failed change, then reconnect. Exercise all browser projects and a stale failed-row dismissal after another tab resumes the operation.
expected: Blocked edits never promise automatic retry. Mixed queues count failed and retryable changes separately. Dismissal preserves resumed/pending work; reconnect applies only the pending edit and leaves the newer peer revision intact.

actions: In an isolated subprocess fixture make the configured helper exit nonzero with quota text on stdout, diagnostic stderr, empty output, and JSON-shaped stdout; also exercise timeout and successful JSON. Then restore an available real helper and resend a paraphrase through the actual composer. This is a guided closure case; no new automated implementation is claimed.
expected: Unsuccessful classifier processes never count as measured decisions or bad-JSON model answers. Bounded diagnostics identify exit/timeout and provider availability. Requests and original IDs remain attributable; the documented fallback is visible. Recovery produces a measured semantic append/update with all source links. Failed helper calls do not silently claim deduplication.

actions: Run matched scratch workloads before and after an optimization with the same provider/model, input files, gate criteria and output checks. Record native-worker and helper calls separately, input/output/cache tokens when reported, task/message growth and elapsed time. Include a completed coordination chain with three quiet board-driver cycles. This is guided measurement, not an existing automated benchmark.
expected: Compare tokens per independently verified outcome, not per message. Quality, semantic target selection, source links and peer review stay equal. Missing provider counters are UNMEASURED, never zero. Duplicate acknowledgement turns cease; claimed savings have baseline and candidate evidence with model/settings and commit identities.
